home.lead: Petrel speaks JMAP, IMAP and POP3. It’s fast, private by default, made for the keyboard, and yours to self-host as a single binary.
home.f1: JMAP for speed, IMAP and POP3 for everything else, SMTP for sending. One inbox for all of them.
home.f2: Remote images and trackers are blocked until you say so. Credentials are encrypted at rest.
home.f3: Gmail-style shortcuts, a command palette, and instant actions with undo.
home.f4: One Go binary with SQLite next to it. Light and dark themes, density settings, English and German.
home.footer: Open source under the MIT license. Built with {tern}.

pgp.title: Encryption
pgp.lead: OpenPGP: encrypt mail so only its recipients can read it, and sign it so they know it’s from you. Petrel keeps your private key locked with your passphrase and opens it for 30 minutes when you enter it.
pgp.generated: Key made. Share your public key, or just write: Petrel sends it along with your mail (Autocrypt).
pgp.deleteConfirm: Delete this key? Mail encrypted to it can’t be read without it.
pgp.lockedHint: Locked: Petrel asks for the passphrase when it needs the key.
pgp.passphraseHint: At least 8 characters. Petrel can’t recover it: without it, mail encrypted to this key can’t be read.
pgp.othersLead: Petrel encrypts to these. It also learns keys from mail that carries them (Autocrypt) and finds keys published by the recipient’s domain.
